meta_description: Convert JPG to WebP to make images smaller for your website. Batch convert in your browser and download a ZIP. No uploads, no sign-up.
subtitle: Make photos lighter for the web. Convert JPG or JPEG images to WebP, one at a time or in a batch, entirely inside your browser.

tool_workspace.description: Drop one or more JPG files below, then click Convert Image.
features_list: Runs in your browser: no uploads

requirements.intro: WebP is an image format from Google built for the web. At similar visual quality it is typically noticeably smaller than JPG, which helps pages load faster and can improve Core Web Vitals.

rows.label: Compression
rows.value: JPG: Lossy: some detail is thrown away each time it is saved. WebP: Lossy or lossless (this tool saves lossy WebP at 90% quality).

rows.label: Transparency
rows.value: JPG: No. Transparent areas become a solid colour. WebP: Yes, including in lossy mode.

rows.label: Best for
rows.value: JPG: Photos, and anywhere that needs maximum compatibility. WebP: Images on websites, where smaller files load faster.

rows.label: Compatibility
rows.value: JPG: Opens everywhere: every browser, phone, app, printer and upload form. WebP: All current browsers. Some older desktop software and some upload forms still reject WebP.

requirements.notes_h3: Before you convert JPG to WebP
notes: Good for: images on your own website or blog, product photos and anywhere page speed matters.
Not ideal for: sending to people who may open it in older software, printing services, or forms that only accept JPG or PNG.
This tool saves WebP at 90% quality. Converting an already compressed JPG adds a second round of compression, so keep the original if you may need it again.
Savings depend on the image: busy, detailed photos shrink less than simple ones.

how_to.title: How to convert JPG to WebP
how_to.step1_text: Select or drag in one or more JPG files. They are read in your browser, not uploaded.
how_to.step2_text: WebP is already selected on this page. You can switch to another format if needed.
how_to.step3_text: Click Convert Image. Each image is redrawn and saved in the new format on your device.
how_to.step4_text: A single image downloads directly; several images download together as a ZIP.

items.q: How much smaller is WebP than JPG?
items.a: It depends on the image. Google reports lossy WebP files are commonly about 25–34% smaller than JPGs of similar quality; your results will vary.
Yes, every current major browser displays WebP. Some older desktop programs and some upload forms still do not accept it.

items.q: Can I convert many images at once?
items.a: Yes. Add multiple files and they download together as a ZIP.
No. Conversion happens locally in your browser.
